title: The Water-Fowl and the Tortoise
logline: A water bird flees his river when birds of prey gather over a dead man, finds a new home and a true friend in a tortoise, then returns to the old bank because the danger seems gone, and a falcon takes him, leaving the tortoise alone.
moral: A danger you can no longer see has not gone away; a safe place and a true friend are worth more than the pull of the old home. (The script states no moral; the film ends on the tortoise alone and shows no moral card.)
tone: Gentle and warm for two thirds (a shy friendship, small comedy from the slow tortoise and the tail-up duck), with quiet dread planted in the pictures (bones, a feather, a shadow), then a sudden, restrained tragedy and a still, sad ending. No gore.

beats.summary: The duck's happy life among the rocks of the wide river.
He sees a dead man on the bank and watches from far away.
Birds of prey come down to the body.
A stone turns out to be a tortoise, who asks why he is sad.
Exile is lighter with a true friend: she offers friendship.
He feels safe and closes his eyes.
He cannot stop thinking of the old home.
She agrees to wait and warns him, looking at the sky.
Only scattered bones remain; the birds are gone.
They go back to the old bank together.
Peaceful days; the fear becomes a memory.
It dives before he can escape.
The tortoise is left alone in the place they chose together.

sets.description: riverShore variant 'rocks', world 1600 x 1230, blue day sky (Library sky + sun at 1250,150). Far bank: Library hillTrees at 0.6 scale on a horizon line y 610. Water band y 610..900 across the full width (blue, Ben-Day dots, three rows of drifting white ripple strokes). Near bank: sand ground with its top at y 900 from x 0 to 1150, sloping to y 960 at x 1260; foreground water fills x 1150..1600 below a water line y 905. Three grey dot-shaded boulders with feet at y 900: x 150 (150 w x 110 h, flat top at y 790, the lookout), x 300 (100 x 70), x 455 (90 x 55, flat top y 845). Reed clump at x 860..1040 (14 stems, 110..150 tall, two brown heads) in a back and a front pass so the body lies between them at x 940. A far rock at x 1300 on the bank (110 x 80) for the third vulture. Bones state: off / on at x 900..1000. Sky can run the planned dayCycle (S16, S19).

riverShore variant 'tree', world 1000 x 1230, Library sky preset 'dawn' (yellow) so it never looks like the old river. Same far bank and water band. Near bank top y 900 from x 0 to 600, sloping to y 960 at x 720, foreground water x 600..1000 (water line y 905) with three lily pads at (760,930), (880,965), (700,985). One Library tree() with its trunk foot at (300,900), top about y 300, and a branch reaching right to x 620 at y 520; roots at x 240..360. The tortoise's 'stone' position is x 220, y 900. No rocks.

props.description: Library worm, in the duck's bill at 7.7.
Library heart, r 26, between the friends at 67.8.

Clean scattered bones in three clusters over 110 units: one rib arc (5 curved ribs on a short spine, 70 wide), two long bones (60 x 10 with knobbed ends, like the bones in the Library den) and four small pieces. Paper white with black brush outline. No skull by default.
Single feather 46 x 14: a leaf shape with a centre quill and three notches; white for the duck, dark brown for the vulture feather among the bones.

subtitles.ar: كان طائر مائي يعيش قرب نهر واسع،|ويحب الهدوء والبحث عن الطعام بين الصخور.|وفي يوم رأى جثة رجل على ضفة النهر،|فوقف بعيدًا يراقب المكان بحذر.
subtitles.en: A water bird lived near a wide river|and enjoyed searching for food among the rocks.|One day he saw a man’s body on the riverbank|and watched cautiously from a distance.

subtitles.ar: تساءل الطائر عما حدث للرجل،|ثم رأى طيورًا جارحة تقترب من الجثة.|خاف أن يصيبه مكروه إذا بقي هناك،|فطار بسرعة بعيدًا عن بيته، حتى وصل إلى نهر آخر.
subtitles.en: The bird wondered what had happened,|then saw birds of prey approaching the body.|Fearing danger if he stayed,|he flew far from home until he reached another river.

subtitles.ar: جلس الطائر قرب شجرة على الماء.|وهناك رأته سلحفاة، وسألته عن سبب حزنه.|أخبرها أنه ترك المكان الذي يعرفه،|وأنه يخشى الأعداء الذين ظهروا فجأة قرب منزله.
subtitles.en: He settled beside a tree at the water.|A tortoise saw him and asked why he was sad.|He explained that he had left his familiar home|and feared enemies who had suddenly appeared nearby.

subtitles.ar: قالت السلحفاة إن الغربة تصبح أهون حين يجد المرء صديقًا صادقًا.|عرضت عليه أن يبقى بقربها، وأن يتحدثا كل يوم.|ارتاح الطائر لكلامها،|وبدأ يشعر بالأمان في المكان الجديد.
subtitles.en: The tortoise said exile was easier with a true friend.|She invited him to stay nearby and talk each day.|Her words comforted him,|and he began to feel safe in his new home.

subtitles.ar: لكن الطائر ظل يفكر في موطنه الأول.|وبعد فترة قال للسلحفاة إنه يريد العودة قليلًا|ليرى هل اختفت الطيور الجارحة.|وافقت على انتظاره، وطلبت منه أن ينتبه إلى الخطر.
subtitles.en: Yet the bird kept thinking of his old home.|After a while he said he wanted to return briefly|to see whether the predators had gone.|The tortoise agreed to wait and urged him to be careful.

subtitles.ar: طار إلى الضفة القديمة، فلم يجد الطيور التي أخافته.|لم يبق من الجثة إلا عظام متناثرة.|شعر أن الخطر انتهى، فعاد إلى السلحفاة وأخبرها بما رأى،|ثم رجعا معًا إلى ذلك المكان.
subtitles.en: He flew to the old bank and found no predators.|Only scattered bones remained.|Thinking the danger was over, he returned to the tortoise and told her what he saw.|They went back together.

subtitles.ar: عاش الصديقان هناك أيامًا هادئة.|كان الطائر يبحث عن طعامه قرب الماء،|وكانت السلحفاة تقضي وقتها إلى جانبه.|وبدا أن خوف الطائر القديم قد أصبح مجرد ذكرى بعيدة.
subtitles.en: The friends spent peaceful days there.|The bird searched for food beside the water,|and the tortoise stayed near him.|His old fear seemed like a distant memory.

subtitles.ar: وفي يوم كان صقر جائع يحلق فوق النهر.|لمح الطائر المائي، فانقض عليه فجأة قبل أن يستطيع الهرب.|قتله وحمله بعيدًا،|وبقيت السلحفاة وحدها في المكان الذي اختاراه معًا.
subtitles.en: One day a hungry falcon flew over the river.|It spotted the water bird and swooped before he could escape.|The falcon killed and carried him away,|leaving the tortoise alone in the place they had chosen together.

new_assets.name: duck
new_assets.description: The planned duck (KD-008), white palette, as this film's hero. Pose fields as planned: fly, flap, ph/amp (waddle), swim, neck (bend down 0..1), headRot, talk, bill (open), wing (gesture angle), wingsUp, plus the shared acting fields. This film adds eyes:'wide' and dabble (see pose).
new_assets.implementation: One function in Library/cast like bird: body ellipse 120 x 80, neck as a 2-point curve whose length and bend come from neck, round head r 30, flat bill 44 x 16 that opens by bill/talk, wing as a teardrop rotating by wing or flapping by flap, orange webbed feet stepped by ph/amp with a +-0.06 body roll for the waddle; eye through eye2/EYE so gaze, lid and wet work; wrap with acting().

new_assets.name: duck dabble (upend)
new_assets.description: dabble 0..1: the duck tips forward until the tail points straight up, the front half hidden below the water line, feet paddling in the air.
new_assets.implementation: Rotate the whole figure about the body centre by dabble * 1.5 rad and clip everything below the water line y; feet use ph for a fast paddle; emit ripple() rings at the water line.

new_assets.name: hawk (bird kind)
new_assets.description: The planned bird of prey kind on the Library bird (hooked beak, heavy brow, talons). This film uses pal 0 falcon (brown, cream barred chest, eye stripe, pointed wings) and pal 1 vulture (dark body, bare pink head, white ruff), plus a silhouette option (all black) for thought clouds and distant shots, and carry (a small shape drawn at the talons).
new_assets.implementation: Add kind 'hawk' to BIRD palettes; draw the beak as a hooked two-curve shape and a brow wedge over the eye; talons as three short claws per foot drawn when fly is true; wings 1.4x the lark's span with a pointed tip; silhouette: fill every part with C.black and skip the eye.

new_assets.name: tortoise acting head, bite and dangle
new_assets.description: The planned optional fields on the Library tortoise (KD-008): neck (extension 0..1), headRot, talk, mouth set (closed, smile, frown, o), brow (negative = worried), front-foot raise. Bite and dangle are not needed here. Defaults must leave the Lion film's tortoise unchanged.
new_assets.implementation: Draw the head on a neck segment whose length is 18 + 40 * neck and rotate the head by headRot; mouth as in turtle; brow as a short stroke above the eye; raise lifts the front foot by an arc of 24 units. Run node Library/tests/regression.mjs afterwards.

new_assets.name: person lie / sit up in bed
new_assets.description: The planned lie pose for the Library person, used only for the still body behind the reeds (no blanket, no pillow, eyes not shown).
new_assets.implementation: Rotate the standing figure by 90 degrees about the feet with arms along the body and one hand turned out; here it is 80 % hidden by the front reed pass, so only the soles and a hand need to read.

new_assets.name: riverShore
new_assets.description: A river seen from its near bank, for any shore fable: far bank on a raised horizon, wide water band, sand bank in front that slopes into foreground water on the right. Options: w (world width), shoreX, sky preset or dayCycle, variant 'rocks' (boulders, reed clump with back and front passes, far rock, bones on/off) and variant 'tree' (one leaning tree, lily pads). Dimensions are in the two set entries.
new_assets.implementation: Bake with bake(): sky(c, preset), hillTrees translated and scaled to the horizon, water as a blue rect with halftone dots; ripple strokes drawn live as a function of t; ground polygon with the slope; boulders as rounded polygons with dot shading on the lower right; reeds as tapered strokes swaying by K.noise(t); tree() from Library/sets. Expose anchor points (rock tops, reed centre, shore line) as constants.

new_assets.name: bones
new_assets.description: Scattered clean bones (rib arc, long bones, small pieces), no skull by default.
new_assets.implementation: Long bones as in the Library den floor (rounded bar with two circles at each end); ribs as 5 concentric arc strokes on a short bar; positions from K.rng with a fixed seed.

new_assets.name: featherFall
new_assets.description: n feathers released at a point at time t0 that rock down on seeded sway paths and come to rest on the ground; also the single still feather prop (white or dark).
new_assets.implementation: Per feather: y = y0 + 60 * (t - t0) eased to the ground, x = x0 + A * sin(w * (t - t0) + phase), rotation following the sway; A, w, phase from K.rng(seed + i); draw a leaf path with a quill line.

new_assets.name: thoughtCloud
new_assets.description: The planned generic thought cloud, used five times (30, 52.9-60.9, 86-88.3, 96-97.3, 143.4-147.2) with small silhouettes or the HOME rocks inside.
new_assets.implementation: cloud() from the Thief film generalised: thoughtCloud(ctx, box, t, drawInside) with three lead-in bubbles toward the thinker and a clip for the inside drawing.

new_assets.name: dayCycle
new_assets.description: The planned sky that runs day, dusk, night, dawn with sun and moon on arcs: two fast passes in S16 and the slow turn to dusk in S19.
new_assets.implementation: Blend the Library sky presets by a phase value and move sun()/a moon disc on a half-ellipse; phase keyed by time.

new_assets.name: groundShadow
new_assets.description: The planned moving shadow of a flying bird on the sand (23.9, 147.8, 152.6-157).
new_assets.implementation: A dark multiply ellipse (alpha 0.25) with a bird-wing outline, positioned from the flyer's x and a fixed ground y, clipped to the ground.

new_assets.name: splash
new_assets.description: The planned crown of drops with rings for the landing at 38.9 and the dabbling.
new_assets.implementation: 8 drops on short ballistic arcs from the entry point plus ripple() rings.

new_assets.name: iconBalloon
new_assets.description: The planned pictogram balloon, single-icon mode twice at 122.8-124.1 (bird of prey crossed out; rocks with a sparkle).
new_assets.implementation: S.box balloon with a tail to the speaker and a callback that draws the icon inside.

new_assets.name: weakFlight
new_assets.description: The planned tired flight in sagging arcs for the arrival at 36.9-38.5.
new_assets.implementation: x linear, y = base + sag * abs(sin) per arc, flap rate rising at the bottom of each arc; returns x, y, flap, rot.

owner_questions: The water bird is drawn as a white duck (the planned 'duck' character); default: duck. A heron or gull is the alternative.
The dead man is shown only as two shoe soles and one hand behind reeds, with no face or wound; default: keep it this mild.
The birds of prey are never shown feeding and the bones have no skull; default: clean bones only.
The falcon's kill is hidden by a white flash and feathers, then a small limp white shape is carried off in far silhouette; default: no blood, no close view.
Additions beyond the script for foreshadowing: one dark feather among the bones, a passing shadow at 147.8, and the tortoise glancing at the sky when she says be careful; default: all included.
Addition: the tortoise sees the falcon first and stamps a silent warning (no lettering) at 157; default: included.
Addition: the tortoise first appears as a 'stone' that pops out a head, and the duck brings her a green shoot in the peaceful days; default: included.

Invented lettering: HOME, BIRDS OF PREY, ANOTHER RIVER, TORTOISE, STAY HERE, SAFE, NEW HOME, OLD HOME, BE CAREFUL!, BIRDS: 0, ALL CLEAR!, HOME AGAIN, FALCON, DAY 1-3, PECK!, FLAP!; default: all used (16 items, which is above the 8-12 lettering diet, so trim on request).
The script gives no moral; default: no moral card, the film ends on the tortoise alone and THE END.
On the trip back the duck walks beside the tortoise instead of flying (the script only says they went back together); default: walking together.
implementation_notes: Screen geography is fixed for the whole film: the old river is to the RIGHT, the new river to the LEFT. He flees right-to-left (S4-S5), returns left-to-right (S11-S12), comes back right-to-left (S13-S14) and the pair walk left-to-right (S14-S15). Never break this.
The two rivers must differ at a glance: old = blue day sky + grey rocks + reeds; new = yellow dawn sky + one big tree + lily pads. Thought clouds of HOME use the blue palette.

Start from Library/template. Use w(p, n) word cues; every cue in this plan gives the Arabic word and its start time. Set LIFE.t = t for automatic blinks and add noBlink on the frozen shocks (10.92, 159.1).
Sizes: duck s 1.0, tortoise s 1.8, vultures s 1.5, falcon s 1.9, body 240 long. Far views (S18 over-shoulder) draw the pair at s 0.25 as simple white and green shapes.
Duck and tortoise eye heights differ; in two-shots use twoShot(duckHead, tortoiseHead, {margin: 90}) and have her stretch her neck (neck 1) while he lowers his.
The body: draw back reeds, then person lie, then front reeds; check on a still that only soles and one hand read. In S12 the bones replace the body at the same x (940).

The strike (161.75): two white frames inside the panel only, then the empty place. Never draw contact, blood or the duck's face after 161.5. The carried shape at 163.26 is a white oval with a hanging neck line, under 40 px on screen.

No effect is placed under the strike because the narration has no gap there; sfx are only at 4.8, 19.2, 19.6, 39.75, 45.0, 51.1, 61.0, 69.8, 76.2, 141.8 and 170.9, all inside listed pauses, with SND master 0.6.
The LATER card covers 88.3-90.1 (words 'wa ba'da fatra'); use the hidden camera key at the card midpoint.
S9, S16 (140.8) and S19 share one side-by-side composition (tortoise left, duck's place right); copy the camera key so the final empty place is felt.
Lettering never covers a face; labels sit in the sky third. No en or em dashes. Subtitles: Noto Naskh Arabic 700, chunks from the subtitles array.
After adding the tortoise fields, the hawk kind and any Library change run node Library/tests/regression.mjs (must say all identical) and rebuild the catalogue.
warnings: Four library additions this film depends on are planned but not built: duck, hawk bird kind, tortoise acting head, thoughtCloud. If the duck is not ready, the Library bird (kind 'y' recoloured white, s 1.6) is a weak fallback: it cannot swim-pose or dabble.
The Library tortoise is small and its face is simple; without the planned head fields the long dialogue S6-S11 will not read. Fallback: the Library turtle on land (it already has talk, brow, mouth).
The ending is a death with no consoling moral; the staging is restrained but the film is sad. See owner_questions.
P8 has no pause between 'escape' (161.50-162.06) and 'killed him' (162.06), so the strike has no sound effect; the flash and shake must carry it.
Lettering count (16) is above the guide's 8-12; the HOME / OLD HOME / NEW HOME labels are the ones that matter for telling the two rivers apart.
